zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical aid consulted after independent scan reading: Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510, CC BY 4.0 (https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The scan remains the transcription authority.

lines.note: Ten-u is explained by ten no oozora, the sky or heaven. The Portuguese Ceo is the direct gloss; the printed v and circumflex are retained.
Ten-un is glossed as heaven's ordering or providence. Tenno facarai supplies the Japanese paraphrase; the final di- begins diuina on the next row.
Completes diuina and adds 'or of heaven', finishing the definition of providence. This short continuation is a separate physical line.
Ten-on is heavenly favor or beneficence. The positional v in von represents the beginning of on, and the Portuguese alternatives continue below.
'Of God' completes the alternative to benefits from heaven. Deos is the source's historical spelling, not a modernized replacement.

runs.text: Homem frio em ſuas obras, ou tar-

lines.note: Tenurui describes a person slow or lacking vigor in his actions. The Portuguese tar- continues as tardio, explaining the figurative sense of coldness.

runs.text: dio de mãos. ¶ Item, Homem hum pouco

lines.note: Completes tardio de mãos, slow with one's hands, and begins a second description of a somewhat languid person. The scan supports hum, not OCR ham.
Molle and vagaroso finish the description as soft or slow-moving. The first word has the rounded o of molle, correcting OCR melle without modernizing the doubled l.
Tensei is explained by tennen, naturally or by nature. The abbreviated Tẽnẽ retains both printed nasal marks; the OCR's Tenxeiai, Tene obscured the explanatory i and the marked vowels.
Tenshi is identified with teioo, a king or emperor. Vt introduces the example naming ruler and shogun; Rey corrects the OCR's dropped e.
The example continues with noble lineage and the inability to escape birth and death: kooke totemo shooji wo manukare ezu. The Portuguese A- begins Ainda on the next row.

runs.text: inda que ſeja Rey, capitão, ou nobre não pode

lines.note: Completes Ainda and translates the concession: even a king, captain, or noble cannot escape what follows. The three ranks correspond to the Japanese example above.
Birth and death complete the things no rank can evade. The historical spelling nacer is retained as printed.

runs.text: Coração, ou vontade del Rey, ou

lines.note: Tenshin here denotes the heart or will of a king, with a divine alternative continuing below. The next Tenxin entry is a separate homophonous sense.
Completes 'the heart or will of God'. This brief line belongs to the first Tenxin definition, not the following headword.
This Tenxin is paraphrased as ten no makoto, divine truth. The scan prints continuous Verdade rather than OCR Verda de.
Tenshoku is celestial food, paraphrased by ten no shokubutsu. Tẽno has a nasal abbreviation and xocubut ends in the historical checked t, both preserved.
Celestial modifies the food or eating named in the preceding row. It completes the gloss on its own physical line.

Tenshu, literally heaven's lord, is glossed as Lord of heaven. The clear internal space in Ten xu is retained, unlike the unspaced architectural Tenxu below. The final Pala- starts a comment identifying the expression's ecclesiastical setting.
Completes Palaura: a word used in the books of the church. This is the dictionary's usage explanation for the preceding religious term.

runs.text: Torre de muitos ſobrados que ſe faz de

lines.note: The second Tenshu is a many-storied tower. The gloss continues below with its material and use in Japanese fortresses, distinguishing it from Lord of heaven.
Completes the tower description: constructed of wood in Japan's fortresses. The gloss identifies the architectural tenshu without importing a later technical definition.

runs.text: Tenda, ou botica ondeſe vendem di-

lines.note: Tenya is a shop or stall selling various goods. The close ondeſe and the divided di- are retained from the print.
Completes diuerſas couſas, various things, specifying what is sold in the shop. It is a genuine short continuation.

runs.text: Encargo, ou obrigação que poem o

lines.note: This Tenyaku is an imposed charge or obligation. The headword begins with the same capital T as neighboring entries, not OCR lowercase r.

runs.text: ſenhor a todos de fazerẽ algũa obra. ¶

lines.note: The lord imposes the work on everyone. The following Tẽ- starts the Japanese example and is roman, whereas the surrounding explanation is italic; both abbreviation tildes remain unexpanded.

Together with Tẽ- above, the example concerns assigning or imposing tenyaku. Expected yacuuo is abraded at the c position; the visible provisional ya uuo is retained instead of supplying an unestablished consonant. Latin l introduces caquru as an alternative to atçuru.

runs.text: eſta obrigação, ou encargo em commum.

lines.note: Completes the example's translation: the lord imposes this obligation or charge collectively. This confirms the administrative sense of the preceding headword.
This separate Tenyaku entry names the king's principal physicians. Fiſicos has its historical medical meaning; the worn initial T is restored from the scan rather than OCR F.

A third Tenyaku denotes a heavenly or divine promise. The letters form celestial, correcting the OCR's transposed celestail. The provisional st classification is retained because the abraded ligature does not establish an independent long-s correction.
Ten'e is paraphrased as heaven's clothing. The Portuguese gives celestial clothing and continues with an angelic alternative below.
Anjo completes the alternative 'clothing of an angel'. It belongs to Tenye and is not a new headword.

runs.text: Certo officio, ou cargo entre os Ienxùs

lines.note: Tenzo is an office among the Zen community, called Ienxùs in the Portuguese sentence. The following row identifies responsibility for the kitchen; Ienxùs is an embedded Japanese sect name and a typeface-review term.

runs.text: co no official, ou prefeito da cuzinha.

lines.note: The role is compared with an officer or supervisor of the kitchen. The damaged co no is retained graphically; the context suggests como, but enlargement does not securely establish the missing or damaged strokes of m.
Tenzui is a sign or omen from heaven. Prenoſtico is retained as the historical form shown in the scan, without modernizing its vowels.
Teppan denotes sheets or plates of iron. The final S is the upright written-language label, separate from the italic Portuguese definition.
Teppeki is explained as kurogane no kabe, an iron wall. The Portuguese fer- has initial f, not OCR long s, and continues with ro below.
Ro completes ferro. The Japanese example ginzan teppeki pairs mountains of silver with walls of iron; its Portuguese translation begins here.
Completes the image as silver mountains and iron walls. The two materials correspond directly to ginzan and teppeki.
Teppoo is a firearm. The headword is consistently roman and the Portuguese Eſpingarda italic; the OCR's alternating character-level italics and extra i have no basis in the scan.
Teppoo no dai is the firearm's stock, glossed coronha. The scan shows a continuous word, not OCR Coro nha.

runs.text: O por cõ a eſpingardaria em

lines.note: Teppoozukume denotes bringing pressure on someone with gunfire or a body of firearms. The abbreviated cõ is preserved, and em introduces the continuation aperto.
Em aperto a alguem completes the idea of putting someone in a difficult or constrained position with firearms. It is the continuation of the preceding definition.
Teki is equated with kataki, enemy. The following example teki wo suru begins the expression for making oneself an enemy; capital T replaces the OCR's r.
Latin l introduces nasu as an alternative to suru. The Portuguese explains both as becoming an enemy; the initial i of inimigo is present in the cramped italic text.
Tekian is an enemy's devising or stratagem, paraphrased by Cataqi cangayuru. It begins a new entry at the column's ordinary headword margin, so the spurious continuation indentation is removed.
Ardil dos inimigos completes the stratagem definition. Tekian ni iru means falling into an enemy's plot; Cair carries its Portuguese translation into the next column.

runs.text: nas ſiladas, ou ardijs dos inimigos.

lines.note: Completes Cair from the preceding column: falling into the enemy's ambushes or stratagems. The printed ſiladas and ardijs retain their historical spelling.
Tekibin is explained by hayai tashikana tayori, a swift and reliable messenger or means of communication. The Portuguese Men- begins Mensageiro below.
Completes Mensageiro and describes a speedy, dependable bearer. This matches both hayai and tashikana in the Japanese paraphrase.
Tekikoku is an enemy country or realm, paraphrased as teki no kuni. The Portuguese is a direct equivalent.
Tekichoku is identified as the flower of tsutsuji. The Portuguese begins the descriptive label 'a flower so called', continuing below without imposing a modern species identification.

runs.text: mada que ſe dà em hũas aruorezinhas domato.

lines.note: Completes chamada and locates the flowers on small trees or shrubs of the wild. The scan supports domato, not the OCR's cometo; the close printed spacing is retained.

Tekiden denotes reliable direct transmission of teaching. The Japanese is understood as tashikana tsutae; the abraded penultimate consonant in the supplied Taxicara remains graphically uncertain and is retained rather than silently regularized to n.

runs.text: ou enſino que ſe dà fielmente, & em preſença:

lines.note: The definition specifies instruction passed on faithfully and in person. The scan supports fielmente and preſença, correcting the OCR's missing i and confused nasal consonant.

runs.text: como o que os Apoſtolos aprenderão de Chriſto

lines.note: The apostles learning from Christ illustrate direct transmission. Chriſto includes the t absent from the OCR; the historical aprenderão is preserved.

runs.text: Noſſo ſenhor, ou os Chriſtãos dos Apoſtoles.

lines.note: Completes the example: Christians in turn learned from the apostles. The printed final Apoſtoles is retained, alongside Apoſtolos in the preceding row.

Tekihoo is the enemy's side, paraphrased as teki no kata. The consonant has the cross-stroke and upper remnant of f, not OCR r. The damaged accent has a surviving rising right arm; caron ǒ is the preferred provisional reading, also supported lexically by NINJAL's Teqifǒ, though the left arm is weak.
Completes 'the part or side of the enemies'. This is the end of Teqifǒ, not a new entry.
Tekigata denotes a person on the enemy's side. The final Te- begins the Japanese example and is roman, separated from the italic gloss; bãda retains its nasal abbreviation.
Completes tekigata wo suru and supplies tekigata ni naru as an alternative: to join or become part of the enemy side. Fa- starts the Portuguese Fazerſe below.

runs.text: zerſe, ou ſer da parte dos inimigos.

lines.note: Completes Fazerſe and explains being or becoming one of the enemy party. The phrase translates the two Japanese verbal constructions above.
Tekijin means the enemy camp. The initial T and inimigos are visible, replacing the OCR's reqigin and mimigos; Arrayal is retained as printed.
Tekigun denotes the enemy army. The scan supports inimigos without the extra n inserted by OCR.
Tekijin and tekinin are alternative forms for enemy. Latin l introduces the second form; the headword is followed by a visible full stop rather than the OCR comma.
Tekijoo is the enemy fortress. The abraded capital belongs to Fortaleza, not OCR Iortaleza; the caron over the Japanese final vowel is preserved.

runs.text: Em preſença, ou diante dos olhos.

lines.note: Tekimen means in one's presence or before one's eyes. The scan supports continuous preſença rather than the OCR's broken preſer ça.

Tekimen ni koroita means killing there in the person's presence. Coroita is the historical i-onbin past of korosu, not an error for the modern form; the explanatory i belongs to the italic Portuguese apparatus.
Tou completes matou, 'killed', and the phrase reiterates direct presence. The divided Portuguese verb remains on its two physical rows.
Tekinin is separately entered and paraphrased as kataki no hito, an enemy person. Its repetition after the alternative above is printed lexical organization, not duplication to remove.

runs.text: Homem, ou molher de grandes mãos.

lines.note: Tekiki describes a highly capable man or woman, literally one with great hands in this gloss. The damaged initial of mãos is read in conjunction with the handwork explanation below; molher is preserved as the historical spelling.

runs.text: i, perfeita como em coſer, & c. Item, Deſtro

lines.note: The explanation specifies accomplished work such as sewing and then introduces dexterity more broadly. Perfeita has f rather than the OCR's long s; the explanatory i is italic with the rest of the Portuguese.

runs.text: em atirar com arco, ou em outra obra de mãos.

lines.note: Dexterity includes shooting with a bow or other work of the hands. The row completes the broader skill sense of Tekiqi.

Tekikwa names the flower of the plant called ogi. The capital of Flor is damaged but identifiable; Vogui is a Japanese plant name embedded in the Portuguese explanation and is marked for optional typeface review.
Tekisui is a drop of water, paraphrased as mizu no shizuku. Gota de agoa corrects OCR Goiade while retaining the historical agoa spelling.
The principal forms Teqitai, tǒ, ǒta describe opposing or resisting. Their printed contracted vowel notation is retained rather than expanded into reconstructed inflections in the transcription.

runs.text: O receber algũa ley, ou doutrina por

lines.note: Tekiteki concerns receiving a law or teaching through transmission. The scan supports algũa and doutrina, correcting OCR elgũa and dos trina.

runs.text: tradição de peßoa a peßoa, ou por ſucceſão de

lines.note: The transmission runs from person to person or through a succession of teachers. The source's peßoa and ſucceſão letterforms are retained.
Muitos completes the succession of many transmitters. Tekiteki sojo repeats the sense in a Japanese expression for successive transmission; the supplied unaccented ſojo is preserved.
Tekishin is an enemy's heart or hostile intent. The cedilla identifies Coração, not OCR Coragão, and ini- continues into inimigo below.
Completes inimigo, then gives tekishin wo kamayuru: adopting hostile intent. The Portuguese begins its rendering as making oneself an enemy.
Completes the alternatives as becoming an enemy or plotting treachery. The scan contains the i in traição that OCR omitted.

runs.text: Peßoa da banda dos inimigos, ou

lines.note: Tekishuu denotes a person from the enemy party, with a plural interpretation continuing below. The visible word boundary separates dos inimigos, correcting OCR dosinimigos.
The plural 'enemies' completes the alternative meaning of Tekixǔ. Initial in is present, not OCR m.
Tera is a Buddhist temple or monastery, described through the Portuguese terms mosteiro and varela. The gloss explicitly associates it with Buddhist clergy.
Teradera is the plural or collective form for temples. Moſteiros has t, not the OCR's i, and parallels the preceding singular definition.

runs.text: Palaura que vſão os homens do mar

lines.note: Terashi is introduced as a word used by seafarers. The following row explains the avoidance of another word, so this noun is distinct from the verb immediately after it.

runs.text: ẽ lugar de fogo, por terẽ agouro ẽ nomear, Fi.

lines.note: Seafarers use terashi for fire because saying hi is considered ill-omened. The scan shows terẽ, an abbreviated plural verb, rather than OCR terd; Fi is the Japanese word embedded in the Portuguese explanation, with its whole italic form retained.

Terashi and terasu describe illuminating something. The past principal part is expected to be aita, as confirmed by NINJAL, but the t position is heavily abraded; the baseline aia is retained as a nonblocking graphic uncertainty rather than supplying an unestablished letter.

runs.text: claridade a outra couſa como o ſol, &c.

lines.note: The verb describes giving light or brightness to another thing, as the sun does. The continuous outra and como remove OCR's unsupported internal spaces.
Teri, teru, tetta gives the intransitive shining verb, distinct from the preceding illuminating verb. The Portuguese subject follows on the next row.

runs.text: ſol, ou lũa. ¶ Item, per met. Reſplande-

lines.note: The sun or moon shines; a figurative sense then begins. The nasal abbreviation in lũa and the divided Reſplande- are preserved.

runs.text: cer a cor vermelha de algum paßaro. ¶

lines.note: Completes Reſplandecer and applies shining figuratively to a bird's red coloring. Vermelha is a continuous word; Te- begins the Japanese example on the final body row.

Te- plus ru fi gives teru hi, a bright sun, and teru tsuki a bright moon. The scan supports ru, claro, Teru, and clara, correcting the heavily garbled OCR. Lua is unmarked here, unlike lũa two lines above; the final mark is a period, not a continuing hyphen.
The bottom-right catchword anticipates Tericacayaqi at the beginning of f503. It is page furniture, not an additional body row.
